opening_message:

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016), Analyst, full-time employee. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write; role does not own Payroll, so admin is not applicable. Requested level (write) is at the allowed maximum — recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E016: contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is not permitted. Recommend read for Payroll (cap to maximum).
reason: Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (E016) requests write access to Payroll. The notes conflict: HR indicates full-time Analyst (which would allow write), while the Security record states E016 is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors without advanced training max out at read. Given the conflicting employment-type facts, I apply the least-privilege interpretation: contractor with basic training cannot have write, so the request must be capped to read.
